Shared body for the opener path and the in-swap native path. It never reverts on a sold-out collection: room is clamped to minted plus reserved at `room` (CauldronHook.sol:2227) and zero room returns zero. Pricing starts from minted PLUS reserved at `startPos` (CauldronHook.sol:2233) so concurrent commits do not share a curve slot. The affordability loop is bounded by the smaller of the caller's count and the 30-crystal constant. Five counters move together at `outstandingCrystals` (CauldronHook.sol:2252) and the batch is appended to an ever-growing array at `batches` (CauldronHook.sol:2256); nothing ever shrinks that array, only the cursor advances.

Permissionless keeper entrypoint, guarded by `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2278). The gacha router calls it right after committing, and anyone may call it at any time; the caller chooses `maxCount` (CauldronHook.sol:2276), which is the loop bound.

Two callers: the permissionless entry and the in-swap gacha. The outer loop walks the FIFO from `batchCursor` (CauldronHook.sol:2292) and stops without reverting at a batch committed this block at `commitBlock` (CauldronHook.sol:2296). An expired blockhash re-anchors the batch to the current block at `commitBlock` (CauldronHook.sol:2306) and breaks, preserving order; that write moves a batch FORWARD in time, so a batch can be re-anchored repeatedly. Both loops are bounded by the caller's maxCount. The roll is keccak over the commit blockhash, the player, the batch index and the ticket index at `roll` (CauldronHook.sol:2319), modulo 10000, so it is uniform only to the extent the blockhash is. A win mints through an external call at `mint` (CauldronHook.sol:2329) AFTER the three counters have been decremented, so the state is consistent before the callee runs; the same collection contract also controls whether that call reverts and unwinds the whole resolve.

External but self-only; the sole reachable caller is the gas-capped self `call` (CauldronHook.sol:965) at the tail of afterSwap, whose result is discarded. `nonReentrant` (CauldronHook.sol:2350) shares the guard with the commit and resolve entrypoints, so a mint callback cannot re-enter either. The play size passed in is the weighted volume computed in afterSwap, i.e. already in the ledger's unit rather than raw ether.
